name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
fundingNote: Up to ₹20L grant for PoC/prototype, plus up to ₹50L as debt or convertible debentures for market entry. Disbursed through empanelled incubators.
cadence: Rolling — apply to an empanelled incubator
summary: The default first stop for DPIIT-recognised, tech-led startups. Money flows through an incubator you pick, in milestone tranches.
eligibility: Incorporated not more than 2 years before applying
Technology used in the core product, business or distribution model
Not more than ₹10L received under other central/state schemes

name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG)
fundingNote: Grant-in-aid up to ₹50L over 18 months, released against milestones via a BIG Partner. Royalty on net sales applies after commercialisation, capped at the grant amount.
cadence: Two calls a year, opening 1 January and 1 July, each open for roughly 45 days
summary: India's flagship idea-to-proof-of-concept grant for biotech. Individuals can apply if incubated; companies need an R&D facility or incubatee status.
eligibility: Company/LLP incorporated within 5 years of the call, at least 51% Indian-owned
Or an Indian-citizen individual incubated at a recognised incubator
In-house R&D facility or incubation arrangement

name: iDEX — Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC)
fundingNote: Grant up to ₹1.5Cr per winner (SPARK framework) for prototype development against a published problem statement.
summary: Pick a problem statement from the armed forces, Coast Guard or DPSUs, build the prototype, and get a path to procurement.
eligibility: Indian startup, MSME or individual innovator
Solution must address a listed problem statement

name: iDEX ADITI
fundingNote: Grant up to 50% of the product development budget, capped at ₹25Cr, for critical and strategic defence technologies.
summary: The deep-tech tier of iDEX for 18–24 month R&D projects with large budgets. Expect a co-funding requirement.
eligibility: Must match a published ADITI challenge
Must fund the remaining share of the development budget

name: iDEX Prime
fundingNote: Grant up to ₹10Cr per project for more mature defence technologies.
summary: A bigger-ticket iDEX track for teams past the early prototype stage.

name: Technology Development Fund (TDF)
fundingNote: Project funding up to ₹50Cr for indigenous defence technology development, against DRDO-published topics.
cadence: Topic-wise calls — check the TDF portal
summary: DRDO-run fund for industry, especially MSMEs and startups, to build defence tech that is currently imported.
eligibility: Proposal must map to a published TDF topic

name: NIDHI-PRAYAS
fundingNote: Up to ₹10L for building a hardware/physical prototype, via a PRAYAS centre (host incubator).
cadence: Each PRAYAS centre runs its own calls
summary: Built for idea-to-prototype hardware work. You don't need a company yet — individuals can apply through a centre.
eligibility: Apply via an approved PRAYAS centre

name: NIDHI Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR)
fundingNote: Monthly fellowship (historically up to ₹30,000/month for up to 12 months) to pursue a venture instead of a job.
summary: Living support for fresh graduates who want to build a tech startup rather than take a placement.
eligibility: Must be incubated at a participating TBI

name: NIDHI Seed Support System (SSS)
fundingNote: Seed support up to ₹1Cr per startup, given by the incubator (often as equity or convertible instrument — check terms).
summary: Incubator-managed seed capital for startups already incubated at a DST-supported TBI.

name: MeitY SAMRIDH
fundingNote: Matching investment up to ₹40L via selected accelerators, alongside acceleration support.
summary: For product startups with traction that want to scale through a MeitY-selected accelerator.

name: MeitY TIDE 2.0
fundingNote: Small grants to ICT startups via TIDE 2.0 incubators (amounts vary by stage — confirm with incubator).
summary: Early support for tech startups working on IoT, AI, blockchain, robotics and similar emerging areas.
eligibility: Tech startup in an emerging-tech area

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
fundingNote: Collateral-free guarantee cover on loans from banks, NBFCs and venture-debt funds. Ceiling was raised in Budget 2025 — confirm the current cap.
summary: Not money from the government — it backs your loan so lenders don't need collateral.
eligibility: Stable revenue and not in default
Loan from a registered member institution

name: Stand-Up India
fundingNote: Bank loans from ₹10L to ₹1Cr for greenfield enterprises.
cadence: Rolling — apply through any scheduled commercial bank
summary: Loans for first-time enterprises led by women or SC/ST founders.
eligibility: At least 51% held by the eligible founder(s)

name: PMEGP
fundingNote: Margin-money subsidy of 15–35% of project cost on a bank loan; project caps differ for manufacturing and services.
summary: Subsidised bank loans for new micro-enterprises; higher subsidy for special categories and rural units.

name: Atal New India Challenge (ANIC)
fundingNote: Grant up to ₹1Cr to commercialise products addressing listed national challenges.
summary: For startups with a working prototype ready to move to market against sector challenges set with ministries.
eligibility: Indian company with a working prototype
Must fit a listed challenge area

name: MSME Idea Hackathon
fundingNote: Up to ₹15L per selected idea, routed through host institutes.
summary: Idea-stage support via host institutes; some editions have been reserved for women founders.
eligibility: Apply through a registered host institute

name: Karnataka Elevate
provider: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Govt. of Karnataka
fundingNote: Grant-in-aid up to ₹50L for selected startups.
summary: Karnataka's main startup grant, with themed editions for women, SC/ST and specific sectors.

name: KSUM Innovation Grants
fundingNote: Tiered grants (idea, productisation, scale-up) — tiers and amounts set per call.
summary: Kerala's staged grants, from first idea to scaling.
eligibility: Stage-appropriate for the tier applied to

name: EIC Accelerator
fundingNote: Grant up to €2.5M (≈₹22–23Cr at current rates) plus optional equity. Non-EU startups generally need to set up in the EU.
summary: Europe's large deep-tech scale-up grant. Worth it only if you're prepared to establish an EU entity.
eligibility: SME established in an EU member state or associated country
